definitions.gloss: three days ago; the day before the day before yesterday
definitions.explanation: Refers to the day that is three days prior to today. Less commonly used than おととい (day before yesterday), but understood in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {一昨昨日|さきおととい}から{熱|ねつ}がある。
examples.english: I've had a fever since three days ago.

examples.japanese: {一昨昨日|さきおととい}{届|とど}いた{荷物|にもつ}をまだ{開|あ}けていない。
examples.english: I still haven't opened the package that arrived three days ago.

examples.japanese: {一昨昨日|さきおととい}の{夜|よる}に{友人|ゆうじん}と{会|あ}ったばかりなのに、もう{懐|なつ}かしい。
examples.english: Even though I just met my friend three nights ago, I already miss them.

notes:
USAGE:
Part of the Japanese system of relative day names: おととい (2 days ago) → {一昨昨日|さきおととい} (3 days ago). Less formal and less commonly used than simply saying {三日前|みっかまえ}. Mostly used in casual conversation.
Some speakers say さきおとつい instead of さきおととい. Both are accepted.

RELATED TIME WORDS:
- {昨日|きのう}: yesterday
- おととい / {一昨日|おととい}: day before yesterday
- {一昨昨日|さきおととい}: three days ago
- {明後日|あさって}: day after tomorrow
